topStories.headline: Irving Street Is Booming. Taraval and Noriega Are Still Treading Water.
topStories.dek: City sales tax data shows the Inner Sunset has blown past its pre-pandemic peak while outer commercial corridors have yet to recover.
topStories.body:
Businesses along Irving Street in the Inner Sunset are reaching record-high sales volumes, driven by a wave of restaurant openings, according to local merchants and city sales tax data reported by Mission Local this week. Businesses in the Inner Sunset are reaching record-high sales volume driven by a boom of restaurant openings; for most of the year, sales tax revenue has grown and is higher than its pre-pandemic levels.

On a recent sunny weekend, the intersection of Ninth Avenue and Irving Street by Golden Gate Park was crowded: parents pushed strollers down the block, people lined up for Arizmendi pizza or Tadaima matcha, and high schoolers sold cookies at every corner. Merchants say restaurants are the engine of that recovery. "We definitely had a lot of vacancies that were filled by restaurants," said Angie Petitt, owner of Sunset Mercantile Emporium. "Food is always a huge destination. People don't need to buy stuff at stores as much as they go out to eat. Our strength seems to be in the restaurants that are opening up."

The picture looks different west of 19th Avenue. Past 19th Avenue, the economy of the Outer Sunset and Parkside areas has not reached pre-pandemic levels, according to the city data, and experienced slight declines in sales tax revenue over the past two years. "Most stores are just maintaining themselves … just paying the bills," said Bill Barnickel, president of the Outer Sunset Merchant & Professional Association.

On Taraval Street, the long-running L-Taraval infrastructure project has left a visible mark. The L-Taraval project has closed some businesses, said Albert Chow, president of People of Parkside Sunset, a neighborhood and merchant group. Chow has been an outspoken critic of the project, and said the loss of parking spots has deterred drivers from frequenting Taraval businesses. With that construction now complete, some residents are hopeful the corridor can rebound. Merchant groups have been experimenting with new events — there are longstanding events like the Inner Sunset Flea Market, which closes two Irving Street blocks every month, but groups have also started new ones, like the Inner Sunset art walk and holiday light strolls, hoping to bring foot traffic to less frequented areas away from Ninth and Irving.

topStories.headline: Fire-Damaged 8th Avenue Apartments Sold for $6.65 Million — and Displaced Tenants Say They Heard Nothing
topStories.dek: The 28-unit Inner Sunset building has stood empty since a 2023 fire, was quietly sold in June, and the handful of tenants with the right to return say no one told them.
topStories.body:
Tenants of a 28-unit apartment complex in the Inner Sunset left their home in a flurry when a fire broke out in 2023 in a hardware store next door and spread to their 100-year-old building. The building has stood empty since then, despite efforts from tenants and city officials to move renovations along. Then, in June, the building was quietly sold to a new owner.

The old landlord, Socrates Mamakos, died in 2025 and his son inherited the property and sold it for $6.65 million in June to a company named Cogs and Dogs Development LLC. The handful of tenants who retain the right to return to their old units were not notified about the sale until Mission Local reached out. "I am totally in the dark," said Chandanie Botejue, a retiree who lived at the apartment complex for 15 years. "Maybe they think we are so inconsequential. They can do this deal and we are kind of pesky and can be tossed aside."

By law, property owners are legally bound to notify tenants in writing about the sale of the building and their rights. The new owner is required to do the same within 30 days of the sale. Notice keeps tenants abreast of a building's progress after a fire because once repairs are completed, landlords have 30 days to alert tenants that they can return, according to the rent board. The law is triggered by the landlord telling tenants that repairs are finished — when this communication doesn't occur, nothing goes into effect.

During two recent visits to the site, a construction worker said a crew of about eight people have been working on the building for four months, with a plan to finish by February 2027. The building is at 1275–1281 8th Ave., at the corner of Irving Street.

topStories.headline: Sunset Dunes or Road Again? Prop G Puts the Great Highway Back Before Voters on November 3
topStories.dek: San Franciscans will vote for a third time in four years on the future of the Upper Great Highway, with a new measure asking to restore weekday car access to what is now Sunset Dunes Park.
topStories.body:
Proposition G asks San Francisco voters to once again pick a side in the years-long parkland-vs.-roadway clash along Ocean Beach. The measure seeks to turn the Upper Great Highway back into a mixed-use area — maintaining parts of Sunset Dunes Park while allowing private vehicle traffic during weekdays.

In November 2024, San Francisco voters approved Prop K, which closed the Upper Great Highway to private vehicles at all times, and the city converted the roadway into Sunset Dunes Park in 2025. Supporters of Prop G submitted 15,924 signatures, and on July 23, 2026, the Department of Elections certified that the petition had more than the 10,615 valid signatures required. The November 2026 measure would reopen the roads between Lincoln Way and Sloat Boulevard to private vehicles on weekdays and restrict vehicle access from 6 p.m. Friday to 4 a.m. Monday and on holidays.

Proponents say the measure takes a balanced approach: traffic congestion in the surrounding neighborhoods will be reduced on busy weekdays, while the park is preserved for its tens of thousands of visitors on weekends and holidays. Opponents say the measure would destroy the existing park, harm the environment, and cost the city millions of dollars. The San Francisco Controller's Office estimates reopening the Upper Great Highway to cars on weekdays would cost $9.8 million in one-time costs and up to $1.9 million annually.

The new Shipwreck Cove children's playground sits on Sunset Dunes Park and would have to be removed if Proposition G reopens the roadway to cars during the week. Friends of Sunset Dunes said a majority of the Board of Supervisors oppose Proposition G, including Board President Rafael Mandelman, Matt Dorsey, Bilal Mahmood, Myrna Melgar, Danny Sauter, and Stephen Sherrill. San Franciscans are voting for the third time in four years on changing the Great Highway. Election Day is November 3.

events.title: Dune Revegetation Volunteer Morning at Sunset Dunes
events.description: SF Rec and Park and Friends of Sunset Dunes host a volunteer session to plant and protect native dune grasses along the oceanfront park. Volunteers have planted more than 2,200 native dune grasses since the park opened.

events.title: Acoustic Happy Hour at Sunset Dunes
events.description: Free outdoor live music on the oceanfront promenade, part of the Friends of Sunset Dunes' regular programming at the park.

events.title: 44th Annual Sandcastle Classic at Ocean Beach
events.location: Ocean Beach at Balboa Street, 1000 Great Highway
events.description: Leap Arts in Education hosts Northern California's largest sandcastle competition, with 100-plus teams of architects, engineers, students, and designers building giant sand sculptures. Free to attend; proceeds support arts programs for Bay Area students.

events.title: Inner Sunset Trick or Treat & Fall Fest
events.location: Irving Street commercial corridor, Inner Sunset
events.description: Local shops hand out treats, a costume parade winds through the neighborhood, and visitors can guess the giant pumpkin's weight to win prizes. Start at the Inner Sunset Farmers' Market at the 8th Avenue entrance to pick up a map.

events.title: 6th Annual Great Hauntway at Sunset Dunes
events.location: Upper Great Highway between Judah and Taraval Streets, Sunset Dunes Park
events.description: Friends of Sunset Dunes' free, family-friendly Halloween event features more than a mile of trick-or-treating, live entertainment, pumpkin decorating, bounce houses, and big bubbles along the oceanfront park. Free and open to all.

events.title: Final Weekend of Ocean Beach Bonfire Season
events.location: Ocean Beach Fire Pits, San Francisco
events.description: The National Park Service's 16 fire rings at Ocean Beach are open for the final weekend of the 2026 season; bonfires are prohibited from November 1 through the end of February. Fire rings are first-come, first-served and fires must be out by 9:30 p.m.

events.title: Inner Sunset Flea Market — Season Finale ('The Big Lunch & Annual Pie Contest')
events.location: Irving Street between 9th and 11th Avenues, Inner Sunset
events.description: The 11th season of the Inner Sunset Flea Market closes out with its annual Pie Contest theme, featuring two blocks of vintage vendors, live music, and free family-friendly activities. Free admission.

moreNews.headline: Abanico Coffee Roasters Opens Second Café at 424 Irving Street
moreNews.body: Abanico Coffee Roasters, the Mission District–based Salvadoran-inspired specialty coffee shop founded by Ana Valle in 2021, has opened a second San Francisco location at 424 Irving St. in the Inner Sunset near Fifth Avenue. The woman-owned roastery sources specialty coffees from across Latin America with a focus on relationships with women producers and describes its new Irving Street spot alongside its original Mission District café. The neighborhood — slower, more walkable, and more family-oriented than the Mission — will be perfect for "a quaint little place to offer a coffee and make people feel at home," Valle said. The space is close to transit stops and foot traffic from UCSF. The shop's own website, as of this week, lists the Inner Sunset location at 424 Irving Street as open for business, with hours coming fall 2026. The storefront previously served as a laundromat and, most recently, as a campaign canvassing office.
